metadata.title: The Influence of Folk Art on Contemporary Artistic and Design Practices
metadata.description:
Abstract: This study aims to examine the influence of folk art and crafts on modern design practices. It will focus on how designers can find innovative ways to apply folk art aesthetic, design languages to evolve and integrate new design languages. The second aspect is how designers can take advantage of technology to achieve desired effects without disturbing the traditional values of the folk arts and crafts. Folk art is deeply rooted in the cultural essence of a region, profoundly influenced by its soil, nature, and geographical characteristics. The close connection between people and their environment is evident in their artistic expressions, where bold and straightforward forms reflect their intrinsic bond with nature. This connection is further exemplified in their vibrant use of colors, linear depictions, and decorative motifs that breathe life into their homes, attire, and everyday objects. The graphic qualities of folk art—its simplicity, charm, and directness—remain fascinating and captivating.
India boasts a rich and diverse tradition of folk art and craft. Each region’s artistic expressions mirror the country’s cultural diversity, shaped by the distinct geographical features of its provinces. Folk art and craft are inseparable from the daily lives of the people, intricately linked to their festivals, rituals, and seasonal changes, which are often tied to agricultural and religious practices. These art forms embody the rhythm of life, weaving together nature and human activity.
For artists and designers, this vibrant lifestyle and its associated art forms—such as dance, music, textiles, pottery, cane work, and geometric crafts—offer a wealth of inspiration. These folk traditions present unique opportunities for exploring functionality, aesthetics, and decoration. The simplification of forms and motifs, particularly of animals, birds, and flora, often serves as a creative foundation for modern interpretations.
This study delves into the inspirational impact of folk art on contemporary artists and illustrators, many of whom have formal training in modern or academic art. Despite their backgrounds, these creators often integrate elements of tribal and folk art into their work, blending these influences with their unique design sensibilities to produce innovative artistic expressions. By analyzing these works, this study uncovers how folk-art traditions resonate within modern creative practices and explores the artistic parameters that define this interaction.
In addition to artistic creations, designers and illustrators have found innovative ways to apply folk aesthetics in communication design. The influence of folk art is evident in advertising, publication design, environmental graphics, outdoor publicity, and editorial illustrations. These contemporary applications demonstrate the enduring relevance of folk aesthetics, as they resonate strongly with the cultural psyche, creating a sense of “Indian-ness” that connects with people across social strata and popular culture. The impact of folk art extends beyond individual creations, influencing the broader field of design education. By studying how artists and designers adapt folk aesthetics, we can identify key inspirational elements that inform modern teaching methodologies.
Practical Implications: Practical exercises based on these findings can be integrated into contemporary design education, fostering a deeper appreciation of folk traditions while equipping students with innovative tools for creative expression. The approach of this study encourages the continuation of folk art’s legacy, ensuring its relevance in modern artistic and design practices. The study not only highlights the cultural significance of these traditions but also offers a roadmap for their integration into the evolving landscape of art and design.

metadata.title: PREDICTIVE MAINTENANCE OF PRODUCTION EQUIPMENT USING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE METHODS
metadata.description: The work provides a comprehensive analysis of modern approaches to predictive maintenance of production equipment using artificial intelligence methods. It examines the features of reactive, preventive, and predictive maintenance strategies, as well as the principles for building predictive maintenance systems. Modern machine learning methods are analyzed, including Random Forest, LSTM, GRU, Isolation Forest, One-Class SVM, and autoencoders, highlighting their advantages, limitations, and suitability for tasks such as classifying equipment condition, predicting remaining equipment life, and detecting anomalies. The typical architecture of predictive maintenance systems has been summarized, and a comparative analysis of modern industrial predictive maintenance platforms has been carried out. Based on a review of the literature, an original qualitative comparison of machine learning methods and a generalized scheme of how predictive maintenance systems function have been developed. It was found that the effectiveness of such systems depends on a combination of quality data preparation, the choice of machine learning algorithms, and architectural decisions. The results obtained can be used as a methodological basis for designing intelligent predictive maintenance systems for production equipment in various industrial sectors.

metadata.title: DIGITAL SCHOLARSHIP AND EMERGING RESEARCH METHODS: THE ROLE OF LIBRARY & COLLABORATION
metadata.description: This presentation examines the growing importance of digital scholarship and emerging research methods in advancing academic research and innovation. It explores the evolving role of libraries in supporting digital research practices, research data management, open science, digital tools, and scholarly communication. The presentation also highlights the value of collaboration among librarians, researchers, institutions, and technology partners in fostering interdisciplinary research, enhancing research visibility, and promoting knowledge creation in the digital age.

metadata.title: CORRUPTION AS AN EXTRAORDINARY CRIME: EVALUATING THE RULE OF LAW, DEMOCRACY AND HUMAN RIGHTS
metadata.description: Corruption categorized as an extraordinary crime continues to show a significant upward trend in Indonesia. As a product of the 1998 reform movement, efforts to realize a clean government were institutionalized through Law Number 28 of 1999. However, empirical realities show a structural anomaly where democratic instruments are hijacked by old power structures acting as free riders to perpetuate authoritarian tendencies. This systemic failure degrades the rule of law and forces a critical re-examination of how political transitions accommodate oligarchic resilience. Consequently, this study addresses how corruption undergoes structural metamorphosis, how state capture interacts with democratic procedures, and to what extent it deprives citizens of constitutional protections. Research Method, using a combined legal research method (normative-empirical jurisprudence) with a qualitative-descriptive approach, this study dissects State Capture Corruption through Olle Törnquist’s "shadowy democracy" thesis and Nils Bubandt's oxymoronic democracy corruption framework. Research Outcome: The results confirm that local oligarchies distort political transitions through the capitalization of authority and Sophistic truth manipulation. This paradox turns democracy into an incubator for systemic corruption, where public funds are diverted, leaving the public as a collective victim. The novelty lies in integrating Samuel Huntington’s transition models to reveal a "transformation from above" using fresh data. Theoretically, it enriches progressive criminal jurisprudence, while practically providing strategic policy recommendations for anti corruption authorities to shield public budgets from oligarchic interventions.

metadata.title: Comparative profitability analysis of land uses between Eucalyptus woodlot and crop production: evidence from Dangila Woreda, Northwest Ethiopia
metadata.description: This study assessed the financial profitability of two land use systems (Eucalyptus versus crop production) in Dangila Woreda, where there is a significant shift toward Eucalyptus woodlots. The expansion of Eucalyptus on arable land competes with food crop production and threatens household food security in the study area. Previously, land use allocation was not based on systematic feasibility assessments. This study evaluated the profitability of the two land uses using financial indicators (NPV and BCR). A multi-stage sampling technique was used to select 316 respondents from four randomly selected kebeles. To evaluate financial profitability, both primary and secondary data were used, including focus group discussions, key informant interviews, and household surveys. The collected data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, t-tests, chi-square tests, trend analysis, and NPV and BCR analyses. The results showed that Eucalyptus woodlot plantations have increased in area over time. The profitability analysis indicated that the Eucalyptus investment generates a significantly higher NPV of 193,978.66 ETB/ha and a BCR of 4.69, whereas crop production yields an NPV of 162,699.13 ETB/ha and a BCR of 1.32. Across sensitivity analysis scenarios, Eucalyptus plantations consistently provide higher net returns and a more favorable return on investment. Despite its higher return, the Eucalyptus planting site must be identified and chosen in consultation with experts to minimize competition with food production.

metadata.title: THE IMPORTANCE OF PEDAGOGICAL APPROACHES AND MODERN TEACHING METHODS IN ARCHITECTURAL EDUCATION
metadata.description: This article examines how the integration of classical pedagogical theories and contemporary digital tools enhances the development of professional competencies among future architects. Architectural education possesses unique characteristics, combining technical knowledge, artistic and aesthetic understanding, creative thinking, and practical skills. The study addresses the following research question: How can established educational theories and innovative technologies be synthesized to improve the quality of architectural pedagogy? The paper discusses the fundamental principles of pedagogy in architectural education, including visual learning, practice-oriented instruction, the development of independent thinking, project-based learning, and the application of digital technologies. Drawing on published case-study evidence on Building Information Modeling (BIM) and Virtual Reality (VR) in design education, the paper argues that digital tools improve learning outcomes only when integrated within the studio sequence rather than taught as stand-alone technical subjects, and concludes with recommendations for curriculum design.
keywords: architectural education; pedagogical approaches; professional competence; project-based learning; creative thinking; innovative technologies; BIM; 3D modeling; practical training; reflective practice; experiential learning.

metadata.title: DIGITAL AND MOTIVATION-BASED HUMAN RESOURCE MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES FOR IMPROVING EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE
metadata.description: This article develops an integrated framework for combining digital HR tools with motivation-based retention strategy and proposes a composite index for tracking its implementation. A review of current practice identifies four recurring weaknesses: bonus schemes that ignore individual differences in what motivates staff, slow adoption of HR analytics for evidence-based decisions, a weak link between training investment and defined career paths, and feedback processes too infrequent to influence behaviour in real time. Building on these findings, the study proposes an indicator architecture spanning four blocks — recruitment and onboarding, learning and development, performance and rewards, and digital HR infrastructure — and constructs a composite employee-engagement index using linear min-max normalisation and a differentially weighted geometric mean. Retrospective estimates for 2019-2025 illustrate how the index responds to specific digital and motivational interventions and where the remaining gaps lie.

metadata.title: Cardiac Autonomic Neuropathy in Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus: A Case Report
metadata.description:
Cardiac Autonomic Neuropathy (CAN) is a well-recognized complication of diabetes mellitus that affects both type 1
and type 2 diabetic patients. Its clinical presentation can be subtle and early detection is of utmost importance for
effective management and prevention of adverse cardiovascular outcomes. We report the case of a 25-year-old male
with an 8-year history of type 1 diabetes who presented with dizziness, worse on standing, together with resting and
orthostatic tachycardia. Several autonomic function tests have been described in literature to confirm the presence and
severity of CAN. However, in an emergency medicine setting common causes of tachycardia (some of them quite
critical) must be excluded before attributing tachycardia to autonomic dysfunction secondary to diabetes. That said,
CAN must always be considered in diabetic patients with relevant clinical presentation as a rule-out diagnosis. This is
particularly important in view of the detrimental cardiovascular sequelae for the patients. In addition, prompt diagnosis
of CAN can have a significant impact on patient’s management by triggering optimization of their diabetic control and
offering treatment that can alleviate their symptoms. CAN is an admittedly challenging complication of diabetes, with
multi-factorial pathogenesis, and largely under-diagnosed with few cases in literature. Further research is needed to
enhance our understanding of CAN and to develop early tools for effective diagnosis of diabetes complication. Thus,
raising awareness among clinicians for this medical entity can prompt early consideration in our differentials and
optimal treatment for the patients.

metadata.title: DIDACTIC FRAMEWORK FOR ENHANCING ENGINEERING STUDENTS' TECHNICAL THINKING COMPETENCE THROUGH SMART LEARNING TECHNOLOGIES
metadata.description: This study examines the didactic framework for enhancing engineering students’ technical thinking competence through smart learning technologies. The research emphasizes competency-based education, digital learning environments, artificial intelligence tools, virtual laboratories, and interactive instructional methods to improve analytical, creative, and problem-solving skills. A pedagogically grounded model is proposed to integrate smart technologies into engineering education, fostering independent learning, technical reasoning, and professional competence. The findings demonstrate that smart learning technologies significantly contribute to developing students’ technical thinking and preparing them for modern engineering practice.
